item.title: What Kawhi Leonard injury update, return timeline means for Raptors
item.description: What Kawhi Leonard injury update, return timeline means for Raptors originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Raptors will be without star forward Kawhi Leonard for a spell. They think they have the pieces to hold them down while he's out. Leonard, acquired via trade during the offseason, is set to be sidelined for a few weeks after hurting his left knee. His latest absence is certainly a blow, although one could argue that Toronto is blessed with a solid number of players to fill his void at his position. With that, here's the latest on Leonard's injury, as well as what it could mean for the Raptors' prospects going forward. What Kawhi Leonard injury update means for Raptors Leonard is set to miss multiple weeks after be found to be experiencing swelling in his left knee, according to ESPN's Shams Charania. The Raptors forward missed Toronto's 117-94 loss to the Timberwolves on Sunday due to the ailment. Leonard, 35, has enjoyed a slow start in his return to Toronto, averaging 19.5 points and 7.5 rebounds on 32.4% shooting. Leonard is averaging 5.5 stocks per game, finding success in head coach Darko Rajakovic's defensive setup. An MRI showed no structural damage to Leonard's knee. Per Charania, both sides will use the time to get the Raptors forward up to speed after his "uncommon investigation" prevented him from joining his team until a resolution was reached on the Clippers ' cap circumvention case. With Leonard on the mend, Toronto is expected to use a replacement-by-committee approach to making up for his lost production. Ja'Kobe Walter took Leonard's place in the starting lineup against Minnesota and performed admirably, producing 22 points on 7-of-12 shooting. Collin Murray-Boyles and Allen Graves should also see additional time with Leonard compromised; they played 19 and 20 minutes against the Timberwolves, respectively. The Raptors prided themselves on their depth entering into the season. Murray-Boyles and Graves are highly-touted defenders with budding offensive games. They should be able to shoulder some of the load while the likes of Scottie Barnes and RJ Barrett are tasked with spearheading the side's two-way disposition with Leonard out. Toronto would obviously prefer to have Leonard be available for selection it the coming few weeks. Still, the Raptors' wing depth suggests that they might be able to keep afloat as their talisman builds his conditioning up after a whirlwind offseason.

item.title: Could Saquon Barkley be traded in Eagles' rebuilding year?
item.description: The NFL trade deadline is quickly approaching. November 10 at 4 p.m. E.T. will mark the end of deal season, at least until Super Bowl 61 is in the books. That's a cutoff that's steadily generated more action in recent years. In-season trades have gone from abnormality to regularity in recent years. It always felt like the Philadelphia Eagles could be active as general manager Howie Roseman sorted through roster moves this fall. But most scenarios had the 2024 Super Bowl champions buying to bolster a playoff run. Instead, it may be the other way around. Philadelphia has lost five straight games after a 2-5 start. All-Pro quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season dealing with blood clots. Future Hall of Fame right tackle Lane Johnson retired. DeVonta Smith has battled injury. So has Saquon Barkley, who could be on the block as Roseman's most valuable trade asset. We've seen him be the booster rocket for a world champion before. Could he be on the move before November 10th? Why the Eagles could trade Barkley It would be one thing if the Philadelphia offense was humming before losing Hurts. Instead, this has been an uninspired attack, somehow worse than last season's. That year, the Eagles ranked 17th in the NFL in expected points added (EPA) per snap and failed to win a playoff game despite winning the NFC East. This year, for the five games Hurts played, that fell to 29th. Swapping out Kevin Patullo for Sean Mannion at offensive coordinator not only didn't fix things, but shattered them to smaller pieces. Barkley was throttled in 2025 but has bounced back admirably in 2026. His 1.8 rushing yards over expected (RYOE) per carry are a career high , though that's in a small 43-handoff sample due to injury and some baffling usage early in the season. He's 29 years old and has plenty of miles on his engine, but is still performing well enough to command a Day 2 draft pick in a trade. Given Roseman's string of draft hits recently, that's enticing. Dealing him would leave about $8 million in dead cap commitments behind this year, which isn't a major concern. Tank Bigsby is currently on injured reserve after surgery to repair a core muscle concern, but he's proven to be an explosive change of pace back in the past; he had 226 RYOE across 2024 (with the Jacksonville Jaguars) and 2025 combined. He could handle duties upon his return, giving the Eagles a chance to decide whether they want to re-sign him when he hits free agency next spring. Why the Eagles wouldn't trade Barkley Barkley is an incredibly important piece of infrastructure, especially for an offense that now belongs to quarterback Tanner McKee. The NFC East is wide open and Philadelphia, even at 2-5, still has valid playoff aspirations. Turning that over to Bigsby, who disappointed in his four games this fall (3.3 yards per carry), would only make things more difficult for the Eagles' offense. item.title: Napoli want Mohamed Ali Zoma, but face tough competition
item.description: Napoli want Mohamed Ali Zoma, but face tough competition As reported by AreaNapoli , Mohamed Ali Zoma is being monitored by several clubs, including Napoli. The 22-year-old looks set to be the next big thing out of Nürnberg, having moved there last summer from AlbinoLeffe. The versatile forward has soon climbed the ranks at the Zweite Bundesliga club and is now an indispensable part of their first XI, having also been chosen by Italy boss Roberto Mancini as part of his young core of players to rebuild the team at the national stage. Capable of playing both centrally and out wide, Zoma has been deployed mostly on the left this season. He already has seven goals this season from nine appearances; last season he managed 14 from 29. TUTTOmercatoWEB reported earlier in the summer that Nürnberg had received offers close to €20 million for him in the final hours of the transfer window, but they wanted more and are expected to at least demand €30 million for his services. Napoli have Zoma on their sights, but they don’t have a free aim at him. Within Italy, they face competition from Roma, while in the Premier League Brentford and Bournemouth have emerged as potential destinations, with Hull City and West Ham having been interested in him in the summer. Big season ahead for Zoma In recent seasons, Nürnberg have gained reputation for being an ideal place for budding forwards, with Can Uzun and Stefanos Tzimas being two of their recent promising exports. Given the way ended last season as well as the manner in which he has started this one, along with the fact that he is an Italy international now, it is highly unlikely Zoma will remain at the club beyond this season. He may even be poached by one of his suitors in January, something Brighton did with Tzimas before loaning him back for the rest of the season. Anshuman Joshi | GIFN

item.title: Why A Former Rally Driver Wrote The Book She Never Had As A Child.
item.description: Nabila Tejpar is a former British Rally Championship Ladies Champion and an advocate for diversity in motorsport. She is now encouraging the next generation of girls into the sport through her children’s book - Racing Towards a Dream. Nabila Tejpar The question she couldn’t answer After Nabila Tejpar appeared on BBC Look East, a young girl spotted her in a supermarket. “That’s the girl who was rallying,” she told her mother. Then she asked Tepjar directly: how did you get started? It should have been an easy question. For Tejpar, it wasn’t, at least not in any way that would help. Her grandfather rallied. Her father rallied. She grew up watching Formula 1 because he did, and standing on the sidelines of Rally GB because he took her. When she decided she wanted to compete, her father showed her how. “My dad told me what to do, and I did it,” she says. “I never had to think about how. I was given the tools.” That honest answer is no use to a child without the family connections. And this situation points to the real barrier in motorsport for many kids, but especially for groups under-represented in the sport. The Inherited Pathway In Tejpar’s experience, the overwhelming majority of people in rallying came in through family, or because they grew up somewhere the sport was part of local life. That holds true for men as much as for women. I call this the Inherited Pathway : in sports with high costs and low visibility, access passes down through families rather than being discovered. Children gravitate towards the sports they can see. They play football and hockey at school. Few ever see a rally car up close. In my work on women’s careers, I describe championing as pivotal for career progression by having access to individuals with influence who activate opportunities on your behalf. Tejpar had a champion, her father opened doors, connected her to the right people and taught her how to pitch herself to corporate sponsors. The question is what happens to the talented child who has no one to do that. A book instead of a lecture Tejpar wanted to show children that motorsport was an option, without building a grassroots programme that might never get off the ground. A children’s book seemed the simplest way to put the idea in front of as many young people as possible. “If some kid sees it, they can look at it and go, ‘Oh, that’s a race car, and that’s a little girl. Now you’re picking up a conversation.” The result is Racing Towards a Dream published in August 2026 by Emrae Publishing. Its hero, Kyla, is a girl of colour who dreams of racing. Tejpar chose the name deliberately, wanting something that could belong to many cultures. She chose racing rather than rallying for the same reason: thanks to Drive to Survive and F1 Academy, children recognise a racing car even if they have never seen a rally stage. item.title: McCarthy, Graham Rave About Steelers Inside Linebackers: ‘Definitely See Growth’
item.description: Oct 25, 2026; Paris, FRA; Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Patrick Queen (6) leaves the field after defeating the New Orleans Saints at Stade de France Stadium. -- Kirby Lee / Imagn Images PITTSBURGH — Pittsburgh Steelers inside linebackers Patrick Queen and Payton Wilson both had banner days in the Steelers’ 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris on Sunday. Wilson had the play of the game with a red zone interception off Tyler Shough, while Queen had a game-high 10 tackles, seven of which were solos, one sack, one tackle for loss, one pass defended and one quarterback hit. “I thought PQ had an excellent week,” Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said during his Monday press conference. “And frankly, we cut him loose on some pressures early, activated him, and gave him a little more ownership in exactly what we’re doing in the player-caller meetings, and things that are going on. So yeah, you definitely see growth.” On a second-and-7 from the Steelers’ 10-yard line, Shough took a two-step drop out of the shotgun and rifled it toward Chris Olave, running a four-yard out to the right. Wilson stayed close by, stretching in front of the pass, squeezing it and somersaulting. “That’s honestly just a credit to our coaches and what we do every day in practice,” Wilson said, sitting in front of reporters. “I’ve repped that play, no lie, more than 20 times now, and Coach Simmo (Jason Simmons), PG ( Patrick Graham ), Scott (McCurley), they all do a really good job of that space away from three, two-by-two. Pretty much all throughout the NFL, that’s where they’re gonna attack, so just gambling a little bit and undercutting it. “Having to defend that play against (Aaron Rodgers) a lot throughout training camp and just in practice has really helped.” Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Payton Wilson during a game against the Detroit Lions on Dec. 21, 2025. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Rodgers revealed a part that Wilson left out. Wilson had picked him off in practice earlier in the week. “I took it all the way back to the house on that one,” Wilson said, laughing and backhanding his quarterback on the shoulder. “The whistles blew, it stopped,” Rodgers said before turning his attention to the next question. Steelers defensive coordinator Patrick Graham said there was more to the story. “There’s more to that. More than the play with Aaron. This goes back to OTAs. This goes back to Phase 2 of training. Space away from 3 when you talk about the 2-by-2 sets and the different tools and different mannerisms in terms of how you get to that space and take that shot. He’s been working on that. That was a really cool moment for both him and the coaching staff. … That’s NFL football. The deeper that story goes, it’s a cool moment.” Queen and Wilson were tabbed as liabilities heading into the season. The duo also had a dreadful game in the team’s Week 4 loss to the Cleveland Browns. Slowly, but surely, the Steelers might have something special brewing with Queen and Wilson,

item.title: Seahawks acquiring Quenton Nelson in trade with Colts
item.description: The Indianapolis Colts have begun their fire sale and it starts with a trade with the Seattle Seahawks involving All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter , the Colts are shipping Nelson off to the Seahawks in what amounts to the first big trade ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline. “Trade: Colts have agreed to send eight-time Pro-Bowl guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks, per me and (Ian Rapoport). Nelson is on an expiring contract and the Colts are opting to get back draft capital now before they could lose him in free agency,” he said. Schefter did not immediately reveal the return for Indy. MORE: NFL MVP odds entering Week 8 of 2026 season Ever since the Colts’ season went into a downward spiral and the team decided to fire general manager Chris Ballard, they have been widely viewed as a top sell candidate. Well, that has now been confirmed. It made sense to move Nelson with the Colts likely set to rebuild. The veteran guard is on the final year of his contract and chances are he would have left in the offseason. Why Seahawks traded for Quenton Nelson Seattle Seahawks general manager John Schneider looks on before a game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High. Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The Seahawks had a clear need at guard during a season in which they are looking to repeat as Super Bowl champs. Nelson fills that need in a big way. The Colts great has been an elite guard in the NFL ever since he entered the league, as evidenced by his eight Pro Bowl nods and six All-Pro selections, three of which were first-team nods. In 2026, Nelson is still playing at an elite level. The 30-year-old has posted Pro Football Focus grades of 85.7 overall, 82.3 in run-blocking and 81.9 in pass-blocking, which rank third, seventh and third among guards. MORE: NFL power rankings entering Week 8 of 2026 season He has not surrendered a single sack and has given up just six pressures in 275 pass-blocking snaps. Now, it’ll be interesting to see how Nelson is deployed. He has played left guard during his career with the Colts, but Grey Zabel, the Seahawks’ 2025 first-round pick, is the starter there in Seattle, so it appears Nelson might be switching sides. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

The Derby della Madonnina is one of the biggest fixtures in Italian football. Unbeaten records at risk An unbeaten record could go in the match with both sides yet to taste defeat in the league. Inter may be the team to beat in Serie A so far this season but Milan have the edge in the derby, having won the last three. item.title: McInnes feels 'guilt' ahead of Hearts return with Rangers
item.description: Derek McInnes left Hearts for Rangers shortly after missing out on the Scottish Premiership title (ANDY BUCHANAN) Rangers boss Derek McInnes said he will understand a hostile reception at Tynecastle despite nearly leading Hearts to a first league title in 66 years last season. The Jambos missed out in the dying minutes of the campaign to Celtic in a final-day shootout for the title. No club other than Celtic and their Glasgow rivals Rangers have been crowned champions of Scotland in 41 years. Within a few weeks Edinburgh side Hearts lost both their manager and captain to Rangers as McInnes followed Scotland striker Lawrence Shankland to Ibrox. The two sides meet for the first time since McInnes's departure on Wednesday, with third-placed Hearts four points adrift of Rangers and eight behind leaders Celtic. "The hope would be that you get on the pitch and clap the fans and there's an acknowledgement both ways, but that's not going to happen. I totally understand that," McInnes said at his pre-match press conference on Tuesday. "I understand that it's not going to be great for me tomorrow, but I get it. "At Hearts, we were hurting. Last season was almost like we were mourning. That might seem a bit exaggerated, but that's how it felt. "We were all clinging to each other during the first part of the close season. It was a time when we felt we should all be sticking together. I felt the guilt about the decision over whether I stayed or left." Hearts led the table for 250 days before being usurped by Celtic on the final day of the campaign as the Hoops won a 14th title in 15 years. To rub salt into Hearts' wounds, they were aggrieved at a number of controversial refereeing decisions that went against them in the final week of the season. "I think there was a real injustice and a grievance towards the end of the season, we felt we should have won the title," added McInnes. "I wanted to be a manager who won a title outside the Old Firm (Celtic and Rangers). But for a few contentious decisions going against us, I think we would have won it." After a slow start, McInnes has turned Rangers around with a nine-game unbeaten run in all competitions. kca/jdg/nf

item.title: Gary Neville drops verdict on Man United's decision to stand by Michael Carrick
item.description: Gary Neville believes Michael Carrick has a difficult task on his hands to get Manchester United’s season back on track after being given more time by the club’s hierarchy. Neville, who captained the club and played with Carrick under Sir Alex Ferguson, sympathises with his former team-mate but sees no quick solution. United's players have managed just two wins from 12 matches in all competitions this season. Before the weekend's defeat against Bournemouth, they had also lost 4-1 at Como in the Champions League. The Bournemouth loss at Old Trafford on Sunday, by three goals to nil, left the side 16th in the table and Carrick arrived at Carrington early on Tuesday morning with his future still uncertain. Training is understood to have taken place as normal, with Carrick and his squad given the chance to turn the situation around and focus on producing a response at Stamford Bridge when his side faces Chelsea in the Premier League this weekend. “I am surprised, but I am happy because I was absolutely certain that what I witnessed on Sunday would be the end of Michael,” Neville said on Sky Sports . Gary Neville admitted he was ‘surprised’ by Man United’s decision (David Davies/PA) (PA Wire) “It looked like he was walking round at the end on his own with the players behind him, like it was almost a goodbye lap, he is waving to the fans to say in almost an apologetic manner, but also a goodbye, so I am really surprised that ultimately Michael is still in a job. “I am happy with it because the fact of the matter is it was very difficult on Sunday. How it is going to go over the next couple of weeks, I have no idea. “But I hope he can get somehow those players to start playing for him again because they haven’t played for him in the last few weeks.” Ashley Young, a former United winger, thinks the club could find it hard to attract a top-level replacement if they eventually part company with Carrick. He said on the Overlap Daily : “For me, the players need to be better, but how many different windows are you going to need to get those players in? “What manager is going to come in and say, ‘I want to work with this squad’? For me, the best manager in the world, Luis Enrique, would look at Manchester United now, look at that squad and say, ‘I’m not touching that. I’m not going there’. “Most managers in the world have seen Manchester United as one of the biggest clubs in the world for years, and at the drop of a hat would have gone to be the manager. Now, I don’t believe that’s the way.” Neville, who played alongside Carrick at United, feels for his former team-mate but believes there is no quick fix ahead.

item.title: Evan Longoria to throw out World Series Game Four first pitch
item.description: ST PETERSBURG, FLORIDA - JULY 12: Former Tampa Bay Rays Player Evan Longoria waves during his #3 retirement at Tropicana Field prior to a game between the Tampa Bay Rays and the Seattle Mariners on July 12, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Julio Aguilar/Getty Images) | Getty Images The greatest player in franchise history, Evan Longoria, will be on hand throw out the ceremonial first pitch before game four of the 2026 World Series between the Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers. Originally drafted by the Rays as the 3rd overall selection of the 2006 draft, Longoria rapidly reached the big leagues by April 2008 and cemented himself as the team’s third baseman for the next decade, completely shattering franchise records along the way. During his 2008 campaign, Longoria became the first player in team history to be awarded the Rookie of the Year. During his 10-year long tenure with the Tampa Bay Rays, Longoria hit .270/.341/.483 with 261 homeruns, registering a 123 wRC+ over 1,435 games played. The first four years of his career, Longoria was on a Hall of Fame trajectory as he averaged 6.7 fWAR per year, but then injuries began to take a toll on his performance. Still, Longoria provided the Rays with solid defense and offensive production throughout the second half of his time with the Rays. In 2011, Evan Longoria provided fans with a lifetime memory when he punched the team’s ticket to the postseason with a walk-off homerun during Game 162 to finalize an incredible month long comeback. To go along with 2008 Rookie of the Year award, Longoria won three Gold Gloves for Tampa Bay and took him a Silver Slugger award in 2009; Longoria also received MVP consideration in six of his 10 seasons with Tampa Bay, placing as high as 6th twice (2010 & 2013). Longoria twice hit three homeruns in a single game and hit for the cycle in 2017, just the second player in franchise history to do so. Following the 2017 season, Longoria was traded to the San Francisco Giants and played decently for five years, averaging 1.4 fWAR per season. Longoria’s last hurrah came in 2023 with the Arizona Diamondbacks, with whom he reached the World Series. Evan Longoria officially retired as a member of the Rays in 2025. Then earlier this year, the Rays retired the #3 and inducted Longoria into the Tampa Bay Rays Hall of Fame.

item.title: Man United took the wrong lesson to leave Michael Carrick with this thankless task
item.description: Manchester United ’s decision-makers took the decision not to make a decision. Perhaps that was typical. If some of their failings in recent years have stemmed from the choices they have made, some have been the result of the times when they did not act. And so, just when it felt inevitable they would sack Michael Carrick , they did not. Carrick was at Carrington on Monday along with chief executive Omar Berrada and sporting director Jason Wilcox. He took training on Tuesday. He will be in charge against Chelsea on Saturday and given the chance to turn an increasingly wretched situation around. It is all the more remarkable as Carrick appeared to have gone beyond the point of no return: on a run of eight games without a win, in consecutive defeats to Como and Bournemouth that were embarrassing surrenders, in a falling-out with Bruno Fernandes that saw the captain criticise the tactics and the manager respond by benching the reigning Footballer of the Year . Perhaps it says something for Carrick’s character that he is still in his post. His calmness and essential decency are reasons why few – with Fernandes seemingly a notable exception – can take offence to him. Whereas Ruben Amorim was seen inside the club as erratic and emotional , the likeable Carrick, with his willingness to assume responsibility, is scarcely a toxic presence. On Friday, he said he was happy to serve as an “umbrella”. He could not shield Wilcox, Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family from derogatory chants on Sunday; but the scrutiny on them would be still greater with a sacking and the confirmation another managerial appointment was a failure. But maybe they took the wrong lessons from the scenes after the final whistle, the choruses of Carrick’s name and the Stretford End’s backing of him, which stood in stark contrast to the boos directed at his feckless players when the manager disappeared from sight. It seemed to come – from the fans anyway – with the implicit understanding it was a goodbye; they appeared to be thanking Carrick, the Geordie who became a United season-ticket holder, the man who made 464 appearances, won five Premier Leagues and played in three Champions League finals, who is a reminder of better times. But when United supporters do not turn on their managers, it does actually rely on the board to dismiss them. And keeping Carrick in situ for a little longer could be giving him a thankless task. If there is little in the performance levels, or the apparent effort of his players , to indicate he will turn this around, the fixture list offers little optimism either. United go to Chelsea next; with a quick turnaround in a Champions League week, there may not be time to act after that. Then they face Roma, then Aston Villa, who are both in form. The cynical interpretation might be that they are sacrificing Carrick in the next three games, not giving him a chance for salvation. item.title: Andrea Ranocchia says Bremer exposed whats happening at Juventus
item.description: Andrea Ranocchia says Bremer exposed whats happening at Juventus Andrea Ranocchia has criticised Gleison Bremer’s public outburst following Juventus’ defeat to Lazio, arguing that the defender should have addressed his teammates privately rather than questioning their effort in a post-match interview. Bremer expressed his frustration after the loss, calling attention to what he perceived as a lack of commitment from his fellow players. His comments attracted attention because of his status as one of Juventus’ most important defenders and a senior figure within the dressing room. Although supporters may understand his frustration given the team’s struggles, publicly criticising teammates can create an uncomfortable situation for a club already under pressure. Juventus have been working to overcome their disappointing results, but Bremer’s remarks have raised questions about how the players are handling their difficulties. Ranocchia questions Bremer’s decision Ranocchia believes Bremer should have kept his criticism within the dressing room instead of making it public. For the former defender, the issue is not necessarily the frustration behind the comments, but the decision to express them in front of the media. Juventus have faced criticism for their performances, and tensions are understandable when results fail to meet expectations. However, disagreements between players are generally expected to be handled internally, particularly when they involve senior figures who carry significant responsibility within the squad. Speaking via Calciomercato , Ranocchia explained why he considered Bremer’s comments a worrying sign for the club. “From inside the locker room, a player like Bremer attacking the locker room… for me those… but in the meantime you say it publicly, in the meantime a player like him can’t say it publicly, you have to say it inside, and that’s a terrible sign for a locker room.” (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) Juventus face questions over dressing room unity Ranocchia’s reaction highlights the potential consequences of airing internal frustrations publicly. While Bremer may have wanted to demand a stronger response from his teammates, his approach risks shifting attention away from the team’s performances and towards relationships within the squad. Juventus have been struggling to find consistency, and the defeat to Lazio added to the scrutiny surrounding their campaign. Maintaining unity will be important as the players attempt to improve their results and respond to criticism. Bremer’s comments do not necessarily prove that the dressing room is divided, but they have created an uncomfortable discussion about how Juventus are managing their current problems. The club will hope the players can address their concerns internally and focus on improving their performances. With pressure continuing to build, resolving any disagreements behind closed doors could help Juventus regain stability and concentrate on their results.

item.title: Natalie Nakase responds to Valkyries being shut out of All-WNBA honors
item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images If Natalie Nakase is losing sleep over the Valkyries missing out on the All-WNBA honors, she certainly isn’t showing it. Plenty of critics wrote off the Valkyries as a nice little regular-season story after they locked up the two seed at 32-12. Going up against the Las Vegas Aces in the semis felt like the end of the line on paper, as Vegas was loaded and heavily favored to run the table. Instead, Golden State went out and completely blew up the script, sweeping the favorites off the floor with relentless team defense. Now sitting with the upper hand in the WNBA Finals against Atlanta, they’ve turned every early doubter into an afterthought. However, the Valkyries still don’t seem to be getting the appreciation that they deserve. When the All-WNBA rosters came out, Golden State got flat-out blanked. Not a single Valkyries player cracked the First or Second team, which felt wild for the league’s number two seed. But Natalie Nakase isn’t letting that affect her Valkyries, as she praised her players. She said: “Our team is our strength. You know, we’ve said strength in numbers and our team about anybody could close, anyone could start, anyone can come off the bench, anyone can finish the game. It’s just so valuable that we can change our rotations. We can change our lineups. That’s what’s kind of dangerous about our team. It’s hard to scout when you have so many options. And so that’s what I love. “And I go back to a common theme of like, I’ve never met 14 players that want to see success in their team that’s sitting to the right or the left. Like no one wants credit on this team. “I said that about Kiah Stokes. Like she gets like, I don’t really want to do too many things. She doesn’t like attention. I think that’s rare. I just think that’s rare in this age with social media and everything is that we have 14 players that really don’t feed into attention, and it keeps us laser focused.” Take a quick glance at their stat sheet and it all makes sense. Gabby Williams topped the squad at just over 14 points a game, with Janelle Salaun and Veronica Burton right on her heels. There’s no ball-hog hunting 30 every night, whoever has the hot hand simply gets the rock. item.title: Texas found something that translates from practice to games
item.description: AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Brad Spence #14 of the Texas Longhorns tackles Trinidad Chambliss #6 of the Ole Miss Rebels in the second quarter at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images AUSTIN — Based on the inability to translate practice work into games from previous weeks , the opening statement from Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian last Thursday wasn’t worth much at the time. “Been really proud of our team this week — they have worked extremely hard,” Sarkisian said during his weekly Zoom call. “Now we need to carry that over to the game, but it wasn’t for lack of effort in in what they put in Monday through Thursday of this week of getting themselves ready for a big-time matchup.” In the wake of Saturday’s 34-27 win over Ole Miss, Sarkisian put into perspective what Texas players actually took from practice into the game to achieve a good defensive performance against one of the nation’s most dangerous offenses. According to the Longhorns head coach, the measurements from the team’s Catapult wearables were at 120 percent compared to the normal baseline during the three midweek practices — Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday. During the game, those measurements reached 125 percent. Texas was straining. “You think about the what our guys exuded all week long, and then what they exuded in that ball game, really proud of them, and proud of the the energy, the effort, the physicality in which they played with, proud of the edge that they played the game with,” Sarkisian said. In meetings with players after the Florida loss, coaches emphasized defensive coordinator Will Muschamp’s “No Thud, No Play” mentality that almost completely shut down the Ole Miss running game. Other than a 34-yard run by Mekhi Frazier in the second quarter on the drive that ended with Texas senior linebacker Rasheem Biles making a goal-line interception on fourth down, the only other run that went for more than 10 yards was the fake punt by Oscar Bird that gained 17 yards. Beyond those two plays, the Rebels carried the ball 27 times for 63 yards, 2.3 yards per carry. One run by Frazier went for 10 yards, but star running back Kewan Lacy only managed 36 yards on 16 carries, right at that 2.3 yards-per-carry mark, prior to leaving the game with a shoulder injury. Sarkisian also cited two scrambles by Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss as evidence of the defense’s effort level. item.title: Kvaratskhelia undergoes knee surgery as rehab spell awaits
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Paris Saint-Germain's Khvicha Kvaratskhelia celebrates scoring his side's first goal during the UEFA Super Cup final soccer match between Aston Villa and Paris Saint-Germain at Stadion Salzburg. (is associated with: «Kvaratskhelia undergoes knee surgery as rehab spell awaits») Adam Davy/PA Wire/dpa Paris Saint-Germain have confirmed winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia has undergone surgery on his torn anterior cruciate ligament and will now start a lengthy period of rehabilitation. Georgia captain Kvaratskhelia suffered the serious knee injury during PSG’s 4-2 Champions League win over Barcelona on October 20. Kvaratskhelia received extensive treatment early in the second half at Parc des Princes following a challenge with Xavi Espart before being helped off by medical staff. A club statement from PGS read: “Khvicha Kvaratskhelia has successfully undergone surgery for a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee at ASPETAR Hospital in Doha, Qatar. He will now begin his rehabilitation.” The 25-year-old is now set for a long spell of recovery, which adds to PSG’s selection problem with France forward Ousmane Dembélé and captain Marquinhos both out because of thigh injuries. Kvaratskhelia has been a key player for PSG over the last few years and has helped the club to back-to-back Champions League titles. Ahead of kick-off at PSG’s home Ligue 1 game against Lyon on Monday night, fans had unfurled a huge banner along the Auteuil Stand with the words “Kvara, the red and blue people are with you” in support of the Georgia winger.
